analysis.title: Poor NVDA
key_insights: NVDA is down about 26% from its October highs, with multiple compression doing most of the damage. The stock is well below its 200-day MA and approaching the $170 support area, with a longer-term trendline just below $170.
The weekend Huang news added to an existing unwind. The report does not state what the news was beyond 'spy allegations' and 'Huang revelations'.
NVDA is at one of its most oversold levels since it was a much smaller stock. The report notes stocks can stay oversold longer than expected.
NVDA 5-day realised vol hit 100 last week, before the spy allegations.
The stock has caught down to the stress signaled by its CDS and is now underperforming credit. CDS spreads stayed relatively calm through November despite the equity decline.

The Market Ear is booking profits on its bearish NVDA trade, first flagged September 23 when implied vol was near pre-COVID lows. The paired AAPL calls versus NVDA puts relative trade is also closed out.

At about 12-13x FY28E earnings, valuation looks increasingly interesting given the growth profile. The de-rating reflects concerns over AI-capex cyclicality, customer concentration and infrastructure financing, not a confirmed fundamental collapse.
The next NVDA earnings report is a key test. If demand holds and financing fears ease, the report sees significant potential for a sharp mean-reversion bounce.

tension_points.bull_case: At 12-13x FY28E earnings with an extraordinary growth profile, valuation is increasingly interesting. If demand holds and financing fears ease, a violent mean-reversion bounce is possible.
tension_points.bear_case: Technical levels are breaking and volatility is exploding. The stock is near the $170 support and trendline, and oversold conditions can persist. Concerns over AI-capex cyclicality, customer concentration and financing remain, plus the Huang headlines.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break below the $170 support area and the longer-term trendline would undercut the bounce case. The next earnings report is the test of demand and financing.
